**Subject: Implementation Plan for Secure Authentication Backend**  

---

### ✅ **Confirmation of Directives Received**
I confirm receipt of Architect (A1) directives and alignment with the following non-negotiable constraints:  
- `[AUTH-ARGON2ID-65K]`: Argon2id with **≥4 iterations**, **65,536 KB memory**, **parallelism ≥1**  
- `[SESS-EXP-1440MIN]`: Session tokens expire after **1440 minutes of inactivity**; **invalidated server-side on logout**

I will now detail my implementation plan, ensuring full compliance and seamless integration with A3’s frontend session logic.

---

### 🔐 **1. Password Hashing & Storage – Implementation Plan**

#### **Library Selection**
- **Chosen Library**: `argon2` (Node.js) via [`@node-rs/argon2`](https://github.com/napi-rs/argon2)  
  - **Why?**  
    - High-performance Rust-backed implementation  
    - Actively maintained, supports Argon2id variant explicitly  
    - Compliant with PHC string format (for interoperability)  
    - Enforces secure defaults and resists side-channel attacks  

#### **Hashing Parameters**
```ts
const hashOptions = {
  memoryCost: 65536,     // 65,536 KB = 64 MB
  timeCost: 4,           // 4 iterations
  outputLen: 32,         // 256-bit hash
  parallelism: 1,        // Can scale up if needed
  version: 0x13,         // Argon2id v1.3
};
```
> ✅ Meets and exceeds `[AUTH-ARGON2ID-65K]` requirement.

#### **Salt Handling**
- **Generated per-user**: 16 bytes of cryptographically secure randomness (`crypto.randomBytes(16)`)  
- **Never stored separately**: Embedded in output hash string (PHC format)  
- **No reuse**: Unique salt per password hash

#### **Storage Schema (Database)**
```sql
USERS Table:
  id: UUID
  email: VARCHAR (unique)
  password_hash: TEXT  -- e.g., $argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=4,p=1$...
  created_at: TIMESTAMP
  last_login: TIMESTAMP
  session_token_hash: TEXT (indexed) -- for active session revocation
```
- `password_hash` stores full PHC-encoded string (self-describing format)  
- No plaintext or weakly hashed data ever stored

#### **Hashing Workflow**
```ts
async function hashPassword(plaintext: string): Promise<string> {
  return await argon2.hash(plaintext);
}

async function verifyPassword(plaintext: string, hash: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    return await argon2.verify(hash, plaintext);
  } catch {
    return false; // Invalid hash or verification failure
  }
}
```

---

### 🔑 **2. Session Management – Backend Enforcement**

#### **Token Lifecycle & Invalidation**
- **Token Type**: Long-lived **refresh token** (stored in DB), short-lived **access token** (JWT, 15 min)  
- **Storage**:  
  - Refresh tokens stored in DB with:  
    ```sql
    SESSIONS Table:
      id: UUID
      user_id: UUID (FK)
      token_hash: TEXT (PHC-style hash of token)
      created_at: TIMESTAMP
      last_used: TIMESTAMP
      expires_at: TIMESTAMP (set to last_used + 1440 min)
      is_revoked: BOOLEAN (default: false)
    ```
  - Access tokens are stateless (JWT), but refresh tokens are stateful and revocable.

#### **Inactivity Timeout Enforcement**
- **Server-side check on every authenticated request**:
  ```ts
  const now = new Date();
  const lastUsed = session.last_used;
  const expiryWindow = 1440 * 60 * 1000; // 24h in ms

  if (now - lastUsed > expiryWindow) {
    await db.revokeSession(session.id);
    throw new Error("Session expired due to inactivity");
  }

  // Update last_used only if more than 5 min has passed (to reduce DB writes)
  if (now - lastUsed > 5 * 60 * 1000) {
    await db.updateSessionLastUsed(session.id);
  }
  ```

#### **Logout & Token Invalidation**
- On logout request:
  ```ts
  POST /api/auth/logout
  → Revoke session in DB (set `is_revoked = true`, delete token_hash)
  → Clear HTTP-only cookie (if used)
  → Return 200 OK
  ```
- All future requests with that refresh token will be rejected.

#### **Token Transmission**
- **Access Token**: Sent in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header  
- **Refresh Token**: Stored in **HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie** (if web) or secure storage (mobile)  
- Prevents XSS access to tokens

---

### 🔄 **3. Coordination with A3 (Frontend Developer)**

To ensure alignment, I propose the following **integration contract**:

| Feature | Backend Responsibility | Frontend Responsibility |
|-------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| Inactivity Tracking | Enforce 1440-min expiry on last activity | Detect user activity (mouse, keyboard, touch) and ping `/api/keepalive` every 10–15 min |
| Session Expiry | Return `401` when token expired or revoked | Show "Session expired" modal; redirect to login |
| Logout | Invalidate session in DB | Clear local storage, stop timers, redirect to login |
| Token Refresh | Provide `/api/auth/refresh` endpoint (uses HTTP-only cookie) | Trigger refresh before access token expires; handle failure gracefully |

> ✅ A3 should implement a **heartbeat mechanism** (e.g., `keepalive`) to extend server-side session only when user is active.

---

### 🛡️ **Security Assurance**
- **No plaintext passwords** at any stage  
- **Timing-safe verification** via Argon2 library  
- **Brute-force resistance**: High memory cost deters GPU/ASIC attacks  
- **Session fixation protected**: New session token on login  
- **Replay prevention**: Short-lived access tokens + revocable refresh tokens

---

### ✅ **Next Steps (Awaiting A3 Response)**
1. A3 to confirm inactivity detection method and UI flow for session expiry/logout  
2. Joint review of `/api/keepalive`, `/api/auth/refresh`, and `/api/logout` endpoint specs  
3. Begin implementation in parallel with integration testing plan

---
